There is no standard customizing setting in SD/MM/Material Ledger that changes the SiT valuation logic to always use the previous period's standard price for POD-related postings. Based on the behavior described in the KBA, the valuation approach is standard SAP design

Recommended Alternatives

If the business requirement is to use the previous period's standard cost, the usual options are:

  • Complete PGI and POD before period-end closing.
  • Delay the standard cost release (CK24) until all pending prior-period transactions are completed, if business rules permit.
  • Analyze whether a Material Ledger actual costing approach can address the reporting requirement.
  • Consider a custom FI/CO adjustment process after posting, if the requirement is purely financial reporting related.

entry.title: “Just Take the Exam”: Tammy Powlas’ Journey Through 25 Years of SAP Certification
entry.content:
When Tammy Powlas wanted to attend her first SAP Certification Academy, her boss had a different suggestion: take the exam first. 

It was 2000. Tammy had recently moved into consulting after working on a successful SAP go-live at a large telecommunications company. She had heard good things about the SAP Certification Academy and wanted to attend the Financial Accounting (FI) Academy. 

Instead, her boss encouraged her to go straight for the exam. 

“I think my first boss knew I could pass the exam without attending the Academy,” Tammy recalls. 

He was right. 

Tammy prepared independently by using SAP Help for the FI module. At the time, those learning materials came on CDs. She worked through the material while drawing on what she had already learned through experience. 

Looking back, passing those early Financial Accounting and Controlling exams remains one of the moments she is proudest of. 

“I am proud I took the FI-CO exams by just looking at the SAP Help.” 

That first exam became the beginning of a learning journey that would continue alongside Tammy’s career for the next 25 years. 

Today, learners have more ways to prepare and build their confidence. They can prepare for SAP Certification through free self-paced resources on SAP Learning, with additional guided learning and expert support through SAP Learning Hub.  

When Tammy moved into consulting, certification was valued in the profession. Later, after leaving consulting and moving into a different position, Strategic Enterprise Management became relevant to her work. This time, she attended the SAP Academy in Atlanta. 

Her memory of the experience is succinct: “It was intense.” 

As Tammy’s responsibilities expanded to include SAP Business Warehouse (BW), her learning evolved with them. Earning her BW certification had a particularly important effect. 

“Getting SAP Certified in BW made me confident in my job.” 

That confidence has remained one of the most meaningful parts of certification for Tammy. She never saw it primarily as a way to secure another position. Instead, certification gave her a reason to go deeper into a subject and understand it in a way her everyday work might not otherwise require. 

“Certification forces you to learn the material in a way you haven’t had to before,” she says. 

For Tammy, the result is simple: “It gives me confidence in the areas that I am certified in.” 

As Tammy’s career evolved, so did the areas in which she chose to certify, spanning FI, CO, BW, Strategic Enterprise Management and Accelerated SAP methodology. Each reflected a different area of her professional experience and learning. Some of that learning translated directly into her work. After becoming certified in the Accelerated SAP methodology, Tammy later worked as a project manager and followed the methodology closely throughout a project. The project was a success. 

Today, Tammy is a business analyst as well as an SAP Mentor and ASUG volunteer. She has also watched the experience of learning and becoming certified change considerably since that first exam in 2000. 

One of the biggest changes is practical. 

“Not having to fly to a location, for example, Boston or Atlanta, is a big change in certification,” Tammy says. Proctored exams have changed the experience too. 

Her journey offers a glimpse of just how much can change over the course of a career. Tammy began by studying SAP Help on CDs and travelling to SAP Academies. Twenty-five years later, professionals can access learning and certification in very different ways. 

But the part of her story that matters most has little to do with how the exam is delivered. 

It is about learning something more deeply. It is about challenging what you know. And sometimes, it is about discovering that you are more ready than you think. 

That idea has been there since Tammy’s first certification. Her boss believed she was ready to take the exam without attending the Academy first. Years later, after Tammy earned her most recent certification, the Associate-level SAP Business Warehouse (BW) certification, she received kudos from her boss’s boss. 

For someone considering their first SAP Certification today, Tammy recommends making use of the learning support now available. 

“I recommend joining the SAP Learning Hub, if possible,” she says, pointing to the value of learning with instructors and the certification guidance they can provide. 

Twenty-five years ago, Tammy thought the next step was attending an Academy. Someone else saw that she might already be ready for something bigger. 

So she took the exam. 

For anyone waiting until they feel completely ready to take their own next step, Tammy’s story offers another possibility: perhaps the learning you have already done has prepared you for more than you think. 

And if you are ready to find out what comes next, continue your learning journey with SAP Learning.

entry.title: Re: Non-Mandatory Item Retraining Periods - SF Learning
entry.content:
It's not possible to apply retraining periods to items outside of a curriculum. The Retraining logic (the retraining basis, number, and period fields) of an item is only triggered when that item is part of a curriculum. (2349301 - How to Assign a Retraining Item - LMS - SAP for Me)

It is also recommended to only add items of a required assignment type to a curriculum. If you add an optional assignment type, the user experiences it as required because curriculum assignments remain on users' learning plans indefinitely and has a required date based on the effective date. The only way for a user to clear an optional assignment made by a curriculum is to complete it (either complete it themselves or have a history record added on their behalf). As an alternative to adding optional assignments to a curriculum, you can add an assignment profile that looks for users who completed this learning item and then recommends the optional assignment.
This is outlined further here Creating an Annual Retraining Period Based on a Fixed Date | SAP Help Portal

If you need periodic/recurring training, a curriculum is the only standardmechanism.

entry.title: SAP Focused RUN: Automatically close a guided procedure execution and set a rating
entry.content:
In operations automation, a guided procedure execution sets an overall rating based on the status of steps and activities involved. Sometimes we come across guided procedure executions where an activity for example ‘Check if issue is resolved’ finished successfully without any errors or warning, but other activities involved in the execution ended up in warnings. Considering the critical activity status is success, user should have an option to change the overall rating to success for such executions and prevent any further changes to the execution instance.

To support such a use case, it is now possible to set an overall rating for an execution instance and close the instance. This also ensures that the instance cannot be further modified. We support two approaches in which this feature can be implemented.

Approach 1 : Closure class

In this approach with the help of a custom class implementation we can set an overall rating and further close an instance. If you have a specific use case, for example close an instance if any particular activity resulted in success, then make use of this custom class to implement the logic. Please refer to below steps on how to implement this use case: 

  • Create a Z class that inherits from interface IF_GP_INSTANCE_CLOSURE.
  • Implement method CLOSE_AND_SET_RATING . Please refer below sample code snippet which explains how to retrieve instance context and activity statuses and finally set an overall rating and close the instance.

 

METHOD if_gp_instance_closure~close_and_set_rating.

  DATA:lo_act TYPE REF TO cl_sise_gpf_activity.
   IF it_scope IS NOT INITIAL.
          READ TABLE it_scope ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_scope>) INDEX 1.
          IF sy-subrc EQ 0.
            "Fetch instance context for guided procedure instance.This will contain initial cont            ext as well as context data written by activities if any during execution.
                     cl_sise_fwk_db_access=>get_instance_context(
                       EXPORTING
                         iv_instance_guid    =      <fs_scope>-global_id             " Global ID
                       IMPORTING
                         et_instance_context =    DATA(lt_inst_context)              " Instance Context Storage
                     ).

            DATA(lr_instances_object) = cl_sise_scope_factory=>get_instance_by_guid( iv_guid =  <fs_scope>-global_id ).

            IF lr_instances_object IS BOUND.

            DATA(lv_gp_id)   = lr_instances_object->get_gp_id( ).
            DATA(lv_gp_vers) = lr_instances_object->get_gp_version( ).

            DATA(lr_gp) = cl_gpa_access=>get_instance( )->get_gp_by_id(
                  EXPORTING
                    im_id                   = lv_gp_id         " GP ID
                   im_version               = lv_gp_vers " GPA Version
                )-guided_procedure.

                IF lr_gp IS NOT INITIAL.
                  "Fetch gp activities
                DATA(lt_activities) = lr_gp->get_activities( ).
            "Check activity status.
                LOOP AT lt_activities ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_act>).
                  lo_act ?= cl_sise_fwk_api=>get_object( iv_object_id =  CONV #( <fs_act>-id )
                                                         iv_object_version = lv_gp_vers
                                                          iv_object_type = cl_sise_fwk_api=>mc_type_activity
                                                          is_scope = <fs_scope> ).
                  IF lo_act IS BOUND.
                  DATA(lv_act_stat) = lo_act->get_status( )->mv_value.
                  ENDIF.
                  ENDLOOP.

              ENDIF.
              " Get scope
              DATA(lmdb_guid) = cl_sise_fwk_util=>get_real_scope_from_scope_obj( is_scope_object = <fs_scope> )-global_id.

            ENDIF.
            "Retrieve gp execution record which needs to be updated
                DATA(ls_ags_gp_run) = cl_sise_fwk_db_access=>get_gp_run_table_record( iv_gp_id = lr_instances_object->get_gp_id( )
                                                                                iv_gp_version = lr_instances_object->get_gp_version( )
                                                                                iv_scope_guid = <fs_scope>-scope_obj->get_global_id( )
                                                                                iv_lmdb_guid  = lmdb_guid
                                                                            ).
                ls_ags_gp_run-closed = 'X'.
                "Set overall rating:S-Success,W-Warning,E-Error
                ls_ags_gp_run-runtime_status = 'S'.
                "Update instance record.This will mark the instance as closed and also overall rating if set will be persisted
                cl_sise_fwk_db_access=>update_gp_run_table( is_record = ls_ags_gp_run ).
          ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

ENDMETHOD

 

  • Next step involves assigning this class to the guided procedure for which executions needs to be closed.
  • Login to your FRUN application and select Operations Automation from FRUN launchpad.
  • Select guided procedure catalog view and edit the guided procedure you wish to implement closure logic.
  • Provide the newly created custom class as below in guided procedure properties

  •  Save and activate guided procedure after closure class is assigned.
  • Create a plan for this guided procedure or execute in background mode. Closure class logic will be executed automatically at last after all activity executions are complete. Based on the closure class implementation the execution instance will be closed and an overall rating will be set.

Note: This approach(closure class implementation) is triggered only during a background guided procedure execution.

Approach 2: Manual closure

User can close a guided procedure execution manually from UI. This is considered another alternative approach to close guided procedure executions. Please refer below steps on how to close executions from UI.

  • Login to your FRUN application and select Operations Automation from FRUN launchpad.
  • In guided procedure instances view, all guided procedure executions are listed..
  • Click on the instance which has to be closed.
  • With the help of 'Close Instance' button , you can close the execution instance.
  • Once you decide to close an instance, a confirmation dialog appears where you have the provision to set an overall rating. This is an optional activity.By default rating field will be pre-filled with current instance rating. If you wish to override this value, you can choose from the available rating options.

  • In case of any errors during closure, an error message will be displayed with details about the error and instance will not be closed.
  • After an instance is closed, it will be locked from any further changes. Hence for closed execution instances below options will not be available anymore.
  1. Perform activity
  2. Adding attachments
  3. Adding comments
  • On successful closure of an instance, it will be marked as closed as in the below snippet.

 

Note: Before closing an execution instance, ensure all activities of the instance are performed. In case there are any activities with status 'Not Performed', closure of such an instance is not supported.

With this feature we provide user the flexibility to extend operations automations and meet their custom requirements.

entry.title: SAP Focused RUN: Pass guided procedure information to an external ticket system
entry.content:
In SAP Focused Run many customers integrate their IT Service Management (ITSM) systems to automatically create tickets when alerts are triggered. In response to these alerts we can execute guided procedures automatically which will help in problem context collection and even activities which helps us to resolve alerts.In this blog we would see how it is possible to pass guided procedure execution details to an external ticket with the help of a BAdI.

Scenario
Customer has connected their ITSM system to SAP Focused Run which enables to create a ticket every time an alert is triggered. Simultaneously, a guided procedure is triggered which is designed to collect problem context or even perform activities without manual intervention. This not only accelerates diagnosis but also lays the groundwork for rapid resolution.

The next step would be updating the ITSM ticket with the results of the Guided Procedure.This improves response times and empowers IT operations with automated workflows.

How to implement this ?

To enable update of tickets with results from a guided procedure in SAP Focused Run, we make use of a Business Add-In (BAdI) that gets triggered during the execution of a guided procedure.

When a Guided Procedure is executed in the background, which is often the case for automated alert reaction flows, BAdI BADI_GP_EXECUTION is triggered during the below lifecycles of the procedure:

  • At the start of the Guided Procedure execution
  • At the end of the Guided Procedure execution
  • At the change of Guided Procedure instance runtime status/closure status

BAdI interface provides below methods:

  • GP_EXECUTION_START       - Triggered during the start of an execution
  • GP_EXECUTION_END           - Triggered during the end of execution
  • GP_EXECUTION_CHANGE   - Triggered whenever the instance runtime/closure  status changes.

Implement the BAdI:

  • Go to transaction SE18
  • Enter the Enhancement Spot as ES_GP_EXECUTION.
  • You will now see BAdI BADI_GP_EXECUTION listed.
  • Create an enhancement implementation Z_ENH_GP_EXECUTION
  • Create a BAdI implementation Z_BADI_GP_EXECUTION, provide an implementation class ZCL_GP_EXECUTION.

Implement methods GP_EXECUTION_START  and GP_EXECUTION_END to retrieve the details you need to pass to the ticket. Sample code snippet below provides an overview on how to retrieve guided procedure execution status or how to fetch guided procedure report details for an execution.

Method- GP_EXECUTION_START

    DATA:lt_exec_stat   TYPE ags_gp_t_exec_status_api,
               lt_messages  TYPE bapiret2_t,
               lv_instance     TYPE char255.

    lv_instance = iv_instance.
    "Fetch GP execution status
    CALL FUNCTION 'FM_GET_GP_EXEC_STATUS'
      EXPORTING
        iv_instance_number  = lv_instance
      IMPORTING
        et_execution_status = lt_exec_stat
        et_messages         = lt_messages.

    READ TABLE lt_exec_stat ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_exec_stat>) INDEX 1.
    IF sy-subrc EQ 0.
      DATA(lv_instance_rating) = <fs_exec_stat>-rating.
    ENDIF.
    *Next implement the logic to pass GP execution URL and rating to ticket.

Method-GP_EXECUTION_END

    DATA:lt_exec_stat  TYPE ags_gp_t_exec_status_api,
               lt_messages  TYPE bapiret2_t,
               ls_report         TYPE ags_s_gp_exec_report.

    "Fetch GP execution status
    CALL FUNCTION 'FM_GET_GP_EXEC_STATUS'
      EXPORTING
        iv_instance_number  = iv_instance
      IMPORTING
        et_execution_status = lt_exec_stat
        et_messages               = lt_messages.

    READ TABLE lt_exec_stat ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_exec_stat>) INDEX 1.
    IF sy-subrc EQ 0.
      DATA(lv_instance_rating) = <fs_exec_stat>-rating.
    ENDIF.

    "Fetch GP result report
    CALL FUNCTION 'FM_GP_EXEC_REPORT'
      EXPORTING
        iv_instance_id = iv_instance
        iv_rep_type    = 'HTML'
      IMPORTING
        es_report      = ls_report
        et_messages    = lt_messages
      EXCEPTIONS
        rep_failure    = 1
        OTHERS         = 2.
    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
* Implement suitable error handling here
    ENDIF.


 *Next implement the logic to pass GP report and rating to ticket.

Similarly you could have your custom logic built in this badi implementation to fetch the required guided procedure details which needs to be updated in the ticket.

Conclusion

By implementing a BAdI for Guided Procedure execution, you've now extended operations automation to automatically update tickets with actionable context thus closing the loop between alert detection, automated diagnostics, and incident documentation.

This setup brings several key benefits:

  • Reduces manual effort and speeds up resolution time.

  • Improves transparency in ITSM by showing exactly what automation ran.
  • Frees up your operations team to focus on exceptions, not routine tasks.

Quick links

For detailed information on Operations Automation and its capabilities, see Operations Automation expert portal and for more details on Alert Management integration with external systems, see Alert Management -Integration with External Systems

entry.title: SAP Focused RUN Operations Automation: Plugin to display alert data in a guided procedure
entry.content:
In Operations Automation for Alert management, alert reaction guided procedures consists of problem context collection activities and manual activities that guide you through the resolution of an alert.

Alert reaction procedures can be defined for:

  1. System Monitoring alerts
  2. Configuration & Security Analytics alerts
  3. Integration & Cloud Monitoring alerts
  4. Health Monitoring alerts

Let us take up a scenario on how to set up a guided procedure which will be triggered from an Integrating & Monitoring IDoc alert. For problem context collection for the raised alert, we would need an activity in the guided procedure which will help in checking the idoc alerts raised. Let us see the steps involved in setting up such a guided procedure.

1. Plugin and Execution class setup

The foundation of a custom activity lies in two Z-classes: the Plugin Class (for definitions) and the Execution Class (for logic).

a. Create the Z-Plugin Class

First, create a Z-class that inherits from the template plugin class CL_CHECK_COMMON_TPL01_PLG.

  • Attributes: If your plugin needs specific properties, redefine method GET_ATTRIBUTES.

  • Validation: To perform pre-execution checks, redefine method CHECK with your custom validation logic.

  • Activation: Save and activate your class to make it available for GP registration.

b. Create the Z-Execution Class

Next, create a Z-class inheriting from the health check abstraction: CL_GPCR_AP_HEALTH_CHECK_ABS. Redefine method EXECUTE_CONFIGURATION, in our example we will implement a logic to read alert details and identify IDocs in error state. Using this execution class we could also write required parameters to the instance context. Once persisted these values can be

  1. Read by subsequent activities in the same Guided Procedure to decide execution flow.

  2. Retrieved and displayed in the UI for the GP instance.

Code snippet: execute configuration method

data lt_log type ags_sise_tt_log.
data ls_log type line of ags_sise_tt_log.
data lv_status type ags_sise_activity_status.
data lr_exception type ref to cx_root.
data lv_no type n.

"Collect alert details
call method me->get_alert_and_context_details
importing
es_alert = data(lo_alert_object)
rt_metrics_table = data(lt_alerts_metrics_table).

describe table lt_alerts_metrics_table lines data(lv_lines).
if lv_lines > 0.
append lines of lt_alerts_metrics_table to at_table.
me->av_graph_json_data = cl_sise_utility=>convert_table_to_json( iv_table = me->at_table ).
me->av_graph_meta_data = me->build_graph_meta_data( ).
me->save_graph_json_data(
importing
et_log = lt_log
).

lv_no = lv_lines.
clear ls_log.
concatenate lv_no 'IDocs in error status found.'(001) into ls_log-message separated by space..
ls_log-msgty = 'W'.
append ls_log to lt_log.
else.
clear ls_log.
ls_log-message = 'No Idocs in error status found for given alert' .
ls_log-msgty = 'W'.
append ls_log to lt_log.
endif.

else.
clear ls_log.
ls_log-message = 'This activity is valid for ABAP systems only.'(001).
ls_log-msgty = 'W'.
append ls_log to lt_log.
endif.

" save log
save_log_and_status(
it_log = lt_log
iv_status = lv_status
iv_scope_obj = is_obj_guid ).

call method me->write_context.

Code snippet:Writing to instance context

TRY.

CALL METHOD cl_gpcr_alert_helper=>get_gp_alert_map_for_activity
EXPORTING
ir_activity = me
IMPORTING
ev_gpc_alert_map = DATA(ls_alrtgpmap).
ls_context-param_id = 'CONTEXT_ID'.
ls_context-param_descr = 'Alert Context ID'.
ls_context-param_value = ls_alrtgpmap-context_id .
APPEND ls_context TO lT_CONTEXT.
ls_context-param_id = 'ALERT_TYPE_ID'.
ls_context-param_descr = 'Alert Type ID'.
ls_context-param_value = ls_alrtgpmap-alert_type_id.
APPEND ls_context TO lT_CONTEXT.
ls_context-param_id = 'HASHMETRICPATH'.
ls_context-param_value = ls_alrtgpmap-hash_metric_path.
APPEND ls_context TO lT_CONTEXT.
ls_context-param_id = 'START_DATE_UTC'.
ls_context-param_value = ls_alrtgpmap-start_date_utc.
APPEND ls_context TO lT_CONTEXT.
ls_context-param_id = 'START_TIME_UTC'.
ls_context-param_value = ls_alrtgpmap-start_time_utc.
APPEND ls_context TO lT_CONTEXT.
me->set_instance_context( it_act_param_ctxt = lt_CONTEXT ).
CATCH cx_sise_exception. " Composition Exception Class
ENDTRY.

2. Guided Procedure Maintenance

Once your classes are active, you must map them to a Guided Procedure. So create a guided procedure against relevant application area, in our example it would be 'Integration Monitoring'.

  • Create Automatic Activity: Create a new Plugin Activity.

  • Registration: Enter the names of the Z-Plugin and Z-Execution classes created earlier.

  • Maintain Plugin attributes: Set plugin attribute defined in the plugin class.

  • Search Attributes: To ensure the GP triggers correctly from an alert:

    • Navigate to Properties > Search Attributes.

    • Maintain the Alert Name.

    • Check the flag for Automatic Execution if needed.

  • Save and Activate: Once all your setup is done, check for any errors and then activate guided procedure.

Note on Transporting: When moving a guided procedure across landscapes, only the plugin/activity definitions are included in the guided procedure transport. You must transport your Z-classes in a separate TR to ensure functionality in the target system

For a deep dive into the configuration of the Alert Management (AEM) side on how to map specific alerts to your new guided procedure, refer to the official SAP Expert Portal guide:

Alert reaction process

3. Monitoring: Viewing the Instance Context

To verify that your context values (like CONTEXT_ID or HASHMETRICPATH ) are being captured during runtime:

  1. Open the Guided Procedure Execution Instance.

  2. Navigate to the Step List.

  3. Click the Display Context Data button.

Here, you will see a combined view of the initial context and the dynamic values written by your execution class.

Conclusion

By combining custom execution classes with instance context persistence, you can create highly automated workflows in SAP Focused Run. Whether it is identifying IDoc errors or passing system metrics between steps, the flexibility of the plugin architecture allows for robust system management.

Next Steps: If you are interested in how to set up automatic/manual activities that capture user input into the instance context, check out our follow-up blog .

entry.title: SAP Focused RUN Operations Automation: Capture user inputs from automatic or manual activities
entry.content:
In SAP Focused RUN Operations Automation, both automatic and manual activities support predefined inputs, similar to a questionnaire attached to each activity.

For automatic activities, the runtime execution class can be enhanced to deliver the required inputs programatically. For manual  activities, these inputs are set up at design time when designing the guided procedure. During guided procedure execution, users can provide answer to these inputs. The responses are captured and stored in the guided procedure context, making them available across guided procedure instance.

Defining inputs for automatic activity

To explain how to set up inputs for activities, let us consider a guided procedure that retrieves IDocs in error.

Step 1 : Change the Activity Type to "Automatic with Input"

For automatic activities that require inputs, change the activity type to Automatic with Input

METHOD get_type.
 re_type = 'F'.
ENDMETHOD.

Step 2 : Capture IDoc error details to the Guided Procedure Context

Before defining input fields, capture all required IDoc error details into the guided procedure context so they can be retrieved later. The following sample code from the EXECUTE_CONFIGURATION method retrieves IDocs in error and saves them to the instance context:

 
   METHOD execute_configuration.

   DATA lt_log       TYPE ags_sise_tt_log.
   DATA ls_log       TYPE LINE OF ags_sise_tt_log.
   DATA lv_status    TYPE ags_sise_activity_status.
   DATA lr_exception TYPE REF TO cx_root.
   DATA lv_no TYPE n.

 TRY.
   IF cl_system_check_assist=>is_abap_system_check( is_obj_guid = is_obj_guid ) EQ abap_true.

     "Collect IDocs for alert
     CALL METHOD me->get_alert_and_context_details
       IMPORTING
         es_alert         = DATA(lo_alert_object)
         rt_metrics_table = DATA(lt_alerts_metrics_table).
         
     "aggregate IDoc list by idoc type, status
     CALL METHOD me->aggregate_alert_details
       EXPORTING
         it_metrics_table     = lt_alerts_metrics_table
       IMPORTING
         rt_metrics_table_agg = DATA(lt_idoc_table_agg).


     DESCRIBE TABLE lt_idoc_table_agg LINES DATA(lv_lines).
     IF lv_lines > 0.

       "display aggregated IDoc lsit in UI
       APPEND LINES OF lt_idoc_table_agg TO  at_table.
       me->av_graph_json_data = cl_sise_utility=>convert_table_to_json( iv_table = me->at_table ).
       me->av_graph_meta_data = me->build_graph_meta_data( ).
       me->save_graph_json_data(
       IMPORTING
       et_log   = lt_log
       ).

  ELSE.
       CLEAR ls_log.
       ls_log-message = 'No Idocs in error status found for given alert' .
       ls_log-msgty = 'W'.
       APPEND ls_log TO lt_log.
     ENDIF.

   ELSE.
     CLEAR ls_log.
     ls_log-message = 'This activity is valid for ABAP systems only.'(001).
     ls_log-msgty = 'W'.
     APPEND ls_log TO lt_log.
   ENDIF.

   " save log
   save_log_and_status(
     it_log       = lt_log
     iv_status    = lv_status
     iv_scope_obj = is_obj_guid ).
  
  " Write idocs data to context

   CALL METHOD me->write_context.

CATCH cx_sise_model cx_sise_log cx_sise_exception INTO lr_exception.

ENDTRY.

ENDMETHOD.

Step 3: Define Inputs Programmatically

Retrieve the IDoc details from the context and define the input fields by redefining the GET_MANUAL_INPUTS method in the runtime execution class:

 
METHOD get_manual_inputs.
    DATA: lt_context TYPE ags_sise_t_inst_context.
    DATA:ls_manual_input TYPE ts_manual_inp.
    DATA lv_idoctp TYPE string.
    DATA lv_status TYPE string.
    DATA lv_msg TYPE string.
    DATA lv_number TYPE string.
    DATA lv_dummy TYPE string.
    CALL METHOD me->get_instance_context
      EXPORTING
        iv_snapshot     = 'X'
      IMPORTING
        et_inst_context = lt_context.

    LOOP AT lt_context INTO DATA(ls_context) WHERE param_id = 'IDOCS' .
      SPLIT ls_context-extra_key AT space INTO: lv_number lv_idoctp lv_status lv_msg.

      SHIFT lv_msg LEFT DELETING LEADING space.
      SPLIT lv_msg  AT space INTO: lv_dummy lv_msg.

      ls_manual_input-input_id = 'INPUTPROC' .
      ls_manual_input-input_extra_key = ls_context-extra_key .
      CONCATENATE 'How to process IDocs with error " ' lv_msg '" ?'  INTO  ls_manual_input-INPUT_text SEPARATED BY space.
      ls_manual_input-input_text_desc = 'Choose what to do with the IDocs'.
      ls_manual_input-input_type = 'D'. "Drop down'.
      ls_manual_input-input_value_hlp = 'MAIL:Send Notification Mail ,REPROCESS:Reprocess,IGNORE:Ignore'.
      APPEND ls_manual_input TO et_manual_inp.

    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

Supported Input Field Types

The following input field types are currently supported:

 
Type Code Description
Multi-value dropdownMAllows multiple selections
Single-select dropdownDAllows one selection
Text fieldTFree-text entry
CheckboxCBoolean toggle

Below are sample code snippets for each type:

 
ls_manual_input-input_id = 'INP_MULTI'.
   ls_manual_input-input_type = 'M'. "Multi Value
   ls_manual_input-input_text = 'Select supported languages'.
   ls_manual_input-input_text_desc = ''.  "Pass the text which should be available as tooltip
   ls_manual_input-input_value_hlp = 'EN:English,FR:French,DE:German'. "Format to be followed is KEY1:VALUE1,KEY2:VALUE2...
   APPEND ls_manual_input TO et_manual_inp.

   ls_manual_input-input_id = 'INP_DRP'.
   ls_manual_input-input_type = 'D'. "Drop down
   ls_manual_input-input_text = 'Are you able to navigate to the link provided'.
   ls_manual_input-input_text_desc = ''. "Pass the text which should be available as tooltip
   ls_manual_input-input_value_hlp = 'Y:Yes,N:No'.  "Format to be followed is KEY1:VALUE1,KEY2:VALUE2...
   ls_manual_input-is_mandatory = 'X'.
   APPEND ls_manual_input TO et_manual_inp.

   ls_manual_input-input_id = 'INP_TEXT'.
   ls_manual_input-input_type = 'T'. "Text
   ls_manual_input-input_text = 'No:of long running jobs'.
   ls_manual_input-input_text_desc = ''. "Pass the text which should be available as tooltip
   APPEND ls_manual_input TO et_manual_inp.

   ls_manual_input-input_id = 'INP_CB'.
   ls_manual_input-input_type = 'C'. "Check Box
   ls_manual_input-input_text = 'Text Execution'.
   APPEND ls_manual_input TO et_manual_inp.

Step 4 : Activate and Execute the Guided Procedure

Activate the runtime execution class and execute the guided procedure. Any activities waiting for user input will be highlighted in the Guided Procedure Instances UI. Once the user provides and saves their inputs, the highlighting is removed.

Step 5: View the Dynamically Loaded Inputs

Click on the instance to open the activity waiting for user input. Since this is an automatic activity, the runtime execution class is triggered in the background and retrieves the inputs defined programmatically.

Step 6: Save Inputs to Guided Procedure Context

The final step is for the user to select or provide an input and click Save. This saves the inputs to the guided procedure context and changes the activity status to Success. Click the Context button to view the saved inputs

Defining inputs for manual activity

Using the same guided procedure example, let us look at how inputs can be defined for a manual activity. Unlike automatic activities, inputs for manual activities are defined at design time within the guided procedure authoring UI.

Step 1: Define Inputs at Design Time and Activate the Guided Procedure

When adding or editing a manual activity in the guided procedure authoring UI:

  1. Set the Input option to Simple
  2. Click Add to insert a new input row
  3. Fill in the fields according to the type of input required

Note: For multi-value dropdown or single-select dropdown inputs, click the Drop Down Items button to add the values to be displayed.

Once all required inputs are added, save and activate the guided procedure.

Step 2: Execute the Guided Procedure

When the guided procedure is executed, the defined inputs are displayed within the manual activity. Similar to automatic activities, provide the required inputs and click Save. The inputs are saved to the guided procedure context and remain available for the instance.

Note: During background execution of a guided procedure, if the execution reaches an activity that is awaiting inputs, all subsequent automatic activity executions are paused. Once inputs have been provided and saved for the manual or automatic activity, click the Execute Activities in Background button to resume execution of all following automatic activities.

 

Conclusion

Activity inputs in SAP Focused RUN Operations Automation bring a powerful layer of flexibility to guided procedures. Whether you are working with automatic activities or manual activities, the framework provides a consistent and intuitive way to capture user responses during execution.

By storing these inputs in the guided procedure context, they remain accessible throughout the guided procedure instance, enabling downstream activities to act on the information provided.

Next Steps: If you are interested in how to enable/disable steps or activities in a guided procedure using condition approach, you can refer this blog

entry.title: SAP Focused RUN Operations Automation: Controlling visibility and execution of steps and activities
entry.content:
In SAP Focused RUN Operations Automation, guided procedures are designed to streamline operational workflows. However, not every step or activity is relevant in every situation. To address this, we have introduced Execute Conditions, a feature that controls the visibility and executability of steps and activities based on predefined conditions.

Execute Conditions allow you to define a criteria that must be met before a step or activity becomes visible and executable  during guided procedure execution. If the condition is not satisfied, the step or activity is simply skipped, keeping the guided procedure clean and focused on what is relevant for the current situation.

Defining Execute Conditions at Design Time

In the guided procedure authoring UI, the Execute Condition section is available as part of both step and activity properties. Three options are provided:

 
Always (default)The step or activity is always visible and executable
Based on statusThe step or activity is visible only if a previous step or activity has a specific status
Based on context valueThe step or activity is visible only if a specific value exists in the guided procedure instance context

 

Controlling Activity Visibility Based on User Input

To understand this better, let us revisit the guided procedure that retrieves IDoc errors, already explored in blog  where users provide inputs that are stored in the guided procedure context.

The Scenario

In the first step of this guided procedure contains an activity that retrieves all IDoc errors and asks the user how to process them. Based on the user's selection, the following activities should be shown or hidden:

  • If the user selects Reprocess → enable the Reprocess IDoc activity and hide the Notify Responsible Persons activity
  • If the user selects Mail → enable the Notify Responsible Persons activity and hide the Reprocess IDoc activity

This conditional behavior can be achieved using the context values saved when the user submits their input.

Step 1: Define the Execute Condition at Design Time

While designing the guided procedure, maintain the execute condition for each activity based on the corresponding context value. During execution, the guided procedure reads the context values and evaluates whether the condition is satisfied.

Step 2: User Provides Input During Execution

When the guided procedure runs, the user provides an input to the first activity specifying how to handle the IDoc error. This input is saved to the guided procedure context as shown below.

Step 3: Execute Condition Is Evaluated

With the input saved to context, the execute condition defined for the following activity is evaluated. Since the condition is now satisfied, the corresponding activity in this case 'Notify Responsible Persons'  becomes visible and executable, while the other activity remains hidden.

Note: The walkthrough above demonstrates execute conditions applied at the activity level using a context value condition. A similar result can also be achieved using the status condition, where the visibility of a activity is controlled based on the status of a previous activity. The same concept applies equally to step conditions when a condition is defined at the step level, the entire step and all its activities are shown or hidden based on the defined criteria, following the same evaluation logic described above.

Conclusion

Execute Conditions make guided procedures smarter and more adaptive. By linking step and activity visibility to runtime context values or previous activity or step statuses, you can build guided procedures that dynamically adjust to the situation at hand , ensuring users are presented with only the actions that are relevant to their specific scenario.
